Until further notice, derived L1 pCO2 data products from this sensor are incorrect and should not be used. A significant discrepancy has been uncovered between the pCO2 values from shipboard water samples vs. values calculated by OOI system. The pco2_pco2wat algorithm is under review and can be viewed at https://github.com/ooici/ion-functions/blob/master/ion_functions/data/co2_functions.py. To receive instant notification of updates to the code, add yourself as a watcher to the GitHub repository linked above. For further questions please email help@oceanobservatories.org.

Analog output from the optodes is produced by using a digital to analog converter (DAC). DAC configuration was initially only done at power up or reset, but firmware version 4.6.4 began updating configuration each time the analog output value was updated to ensure long-term continuous operation. Unfortunately, this also produced a voltage jump, creating erratic noise in the output data. The firmware has been corrected, but only the onboard-calculated Stern-Volmer values [DO from Onboard Calculation (L1 product; 'ctd_tc_oxygen') and DO from Onboard Calculation - Corrected (L2 product; 'dissolved_oxygen')] should be used during this annotated time range, NOT the 'DO from Phase' data which contain the noisy analog signal.

Camera has been repeatedly going into error states with 'camera_3' errors and data storage becoming unavailable. The node PC01A node swap that occurred during VISIONS24 replaced VADCPA101 (RDI Workhorse) with the new VADCPB101 (Nortek Signature 500).

Digi timestamps were not enabled, which is likely why data were not appearing in the proper places. They have now been enabled. Instrument was responsive and Mission Execution appears to be running normally, though there were some interruptions in mission execution earlier in this period.

Due to a known issue with the code that allows interpolation of 2D parameters, the vertical 5th beam data are not being pulled in to calculate the 'Upward Turbulent Seawater Velocity - True' values. That parameter is currently filled with NaN values while the fix is in progress. An update will be issued when the code is corrected on production.

Following a chiller changeover after a regular maintenance check, a low flow to High Voltage Power Supply (HVPS) Nos. 1 and 2 caused the system to power down. Wiring was inspected by vendor, a 5-second delay scenario was removed, and all deployed primary and secondary infrastructure are now back online.

Camera data storage was not reachable and camera was showing Camera_3 error when taking photos. Rebooted but could not reconnect via Rayfin software, so power cycled camera. Camera operating normally following power cycle.
Instrument not reporting data because polling was not enabled in the logger for unknown reasons. It has now been re-enabled.
Camera has not been taking photos since 6 Nov. Camera was rebooted and is back online.

Following missing data alerts, the instrument was power cycled and relaunched. Instrument has a large ground fault (339,-50) and current is high (75 mA) when serial port is connected. While it is responsive and outputting data, the data are not valid. Instrument has been powered down, marked as failed and alarms silenced.

On Dec 11 at 0636 PT, shore station Chiller No. 2 pump failure caused the system to power down. Maintenance vendor testing could not identify an issue and the failure was not able to be recreated. Power feed equipment was energized and the North and South cables re-powered, followed by the deployed infrastructure.

A lightning strike close to the shore station resulted in the opening of the HV breakers feeding the cables. The PFE was secured and visual inspections performed to ensure there was no equipment damage. System lightning protection performed as expected and power was restored and instruments started back up within 10 hours.

Attempted reboot and reconnect to media folders, but data storage would not mount. Camera offline until successful reboot and remounting of data storage regained access to image files on 2025-02-19.

Platform ADCPs (RDI; 150 kHz) appear to cause interference in VADCP (Nortek Signature500; 500 kHz) data based on previous spectrum measurements made using vendor software. We temporarily stopped platform ADCPs from pinging (while remaining powered on) to analyze the quality of VADCP data without interference from ADCPs. Profilers remained in normal mission mode.

Paused at 170m to diagnose a levelwind current spike & winch/levelwind rpm oscillation on descent almost every profile. Instruments sampling via mission execution (nitrate, pCO2, and pH) were paused during this period. Seems to be related to cable wrap/side-loading issues. The trip occurs at a safe depth, so normal profiling was resumed and we will assess alternate solutions (e.g. adjusting profile) if the trip occurs again.

Profiler aborted profiling again due to excessive levelwind current at 170m. Cameras observed a cross-over spanning 3 or 4 wraps, which was likely the cause of the current trip, and visible damage to the EM cable. Profiler was brought down to parking position for investigation. Only 1 VDSL pair is communicating when docked and communications become intermittent when undocked, leading to unreliable depth data and sparse instrument data. The profiler remained parked with instruments powered on (except those sampling via mission execution: nitrate, pCO2, and pH) while contingencies were discussed.
Profiler was extended to 100m depth to try to work out any twists in the cable causing the misaligned wraps and levelwind excessive current trips.

After about 160hrs at 100m, pod was retracted to parking position. Same miswrap issues & winch/levelwind current oscillations were seen, so the retract speed was reduced from 400 rpm to 250 rpm. This initially seemed to help, so further testing was conducted under that configuration. Profiles ran intermittently while testing was performed.
All cabled instruments were temporarily powered down to replace 14-year-old out of band switches at the shore station.

Reduced bin size from 1 m to 0.5 m and increased from 70 to 100 bins due to decreased signal beyond 45-50 m from the instrument. If successful, the next deployment will likely use these values as well.

HITL review found an interesting possible upwelling event and subsequent plankton bloom at Slope Base during this time period. Elevated nitrate, chlA, and pCO2 levels (along with increased echo intensity in the ADCP data) coincide with a decrease in temperature, pH, and oxygen, indicating a potential increase in productivity spurred by upwelling of deep, cold, nutrient-rich water.

The 01A profiler at Slope Base tripped on 18 July at 18:23 UTC with no indicated cause from the mechanical system logs. This may be related to the unexpected reboot of one of the routing switches at the shore station. One backhaul circuit lost connectivity as a result, but the switch is clustered with another that took the traffic, so there was no loss of data. Profiler pod returned to mission mode on 22 July at 21:07 UTC.

During the initial cable stretching upcast following deployment the platform port powered down and the profiler pod lost power. There appears to have been a communications issue with the newly deployed controller can. The 2024-2025 SC01B was redeployed in place of SC01A.

Instrument was sending late data notifications and had a port overcurrent immediately after deployment and was marked as failed. However, it returned to an operational state after a profiler science pod overcurrent event and reset. Mechanism for restoration is under investigation, but data appear reasonable.
Checked and updated Aquadopp instruments, which were found to be running at Low+ power setting instead of High power.  Instruments have been updated to run at high power, 1 Hz sampling, ENU format.

The SC01A expansion port in PC01A overcurrented after the SciP saw a 7.6 m depth fluctuation at ~30m deep about 5 seconds after turning around at the top of the profile. Pod was retracted, winch encoders were reset, and normal profiling resumed at 20:43 UTC.

The camera controller has been scheduled to reboot the camera between collection cycles daily at 1830 UTC. This is being implemented on an experimental basis to attempt to reduce instances of API connection errors on the cameras.

HITL review found an interesting turbulent event at the Slope Base Shallow Profiler site during this time period characterized by increased temperature, salinity, nitrate, chlA, CDOM, and pCO2 (along with increased fluorometer backscatter and ADCP echo intensity) and decreases in pH and oxygen levels relative to climatologies. The tail end of the event coincided with a profiler blowdown event that extended from ~0700 UTC on 23 Jan to ~1900 on 27 Jan.

A network interruption following a DAS experiment stopped the profiler unexpectedly during an upcast. The pod was stuck at ~20 m water depth until the profiler could be retracted and returned to mission mode.
